briefs.headline: Mild earthquake strikes Doddaballapura in Bengaluru, residents safe
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Residents across several villages in Tubagere hobli, located in Doddaballapura taluk of Bengaluru Rural district, experienced mild earthquake tremors Friday morning.
According to seismic monitoring reports, the earthquake struck at 9:02am with a magnitude of 3.0 on the 
Richter scale
. The epicentre was pinpointed, with a focal depth recorded at approximately 10 kilometres below the earth’s surface.
The sudden vibrations sparked momentary panic among villagers who were going about their morning routine. Many locals said they heard a loud, rumbling noise from their roofs just as the ground began to vibrate.
“We were inside our homes when we suddenly heard a loud sound followed by the ground trembling beneath us. Fortunately, it lasted only a few seconds and no damage occurred,” said a resident from Tubagere.
Authorities and emergency services confirmed there have been no reports of structural damage to houses or to public infrastructure, or of injuries to livestock and residents. Local administration officials are monitoring the situation in surrounding villages as a precautionary measure.

briefs.headline: Rail passengers seek SMVT station improvement, better connectivity in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Rail passengers Thursday expressed their concerns about the poor upkeep of Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminus (SMVT) at Byappanahalli. As part of the Rail Jan Samvad programme, several passengers at the city’s railway stations were asked to share their feedback and demands with officials of South Western Railway (SWR).
At KSR Bengaluru, divisional railway manager (DRM) Ashutosh Kumar Singh interacted with passengers. The feedback and responses, documented by SWR officials, are expected to be used internally for improvements.
Rail activist Krishnaprasad KN stated that poor upkeep and inadequate accessibility have plagued SMVT since inception. “The condition there is very bad, but he (DRM) says it is good... It is not accessible for those in south Bengaluru and cleanliness has gone for a toss,” he explained.
Passengers also demanded additional platforms at KSR Bengaluru. Sreedhar, a passenger, sought additional connectivity towards Shivamogga and more platforms at Yeshwantpur railway station.
Responding to the queries, Singh claimed that passengers are happy with SMVT. However, he acknowledged that it needs to improve on its connectivity and that the upcoming rotary flyover at IOC Junction can solve it.
“The connectivity of SMVT is obviously not very good but now GBA is making the rotary flyover. 
Once the rotary flyover is done, the connectivity will be improved,” the DRM explained.
Singh further added that while passengers want new trains to be introduced from KSR or Yeshwantpur stations, the railways has technical limitations at these two stations. “Whenever we introduce new trains, we take into consideration the feasibility, maintenance facility, platform availability etc. Based on this, we start the trains,” he said.

briefs.headline: Retired excise guard, daughter jailed in Bengaluru in money laundering case
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A retired excise guard and his daughter have been sentenced to rigorous imprisonment in a money-laundering case.
A special court, which pronounced the judgment on Oct 14, also ordered the confiscation of five properties and directed the registration of a separate perjury case against a defence witness for giving false testimony during the trial.
Directorate of Enforcement (ED) secured the conviction of M Ramachandra, a retired excise guard who had served as an in-charge sub-inspector, and his daughter, R Yurekha, under Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
The court sentenced Ramachandra to five years of rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh. In case of default of payment, he will undergo two years of simple imprisonment. Yurekha was sentenced to three years of rigorous imprisonment and fined Rs 3 lakh, with an additional year of simple imprisonment in case of default.
The case originated from an FIR registered by Lokayukta police in 2009, following allegations that Ramachandra had assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.
Ramachandra used his powers to obtain an excise licence in Yurekha’s name. In 2001, when Yurekha was in college, Kwality Wine Centre was opened at Chamarajpet. He also purchased land in Hunsur and Yelahanka in Yurekha’s name using the proceeds of crime.
In March 2016, ED provisionally attached eight properties valued at Rs 1 crore and filed its prosecution complaint in June that year.
In the underlying disproportionate assets case, the trial court, in a judgment delivered on Nov 8, 2024, convicted Ramachandra under Prevention of Corruption Act. He was sentenced to three years of rigorous imprisonment and fined Rs 50 lakh. The court assessed his disproportionate assets at Rs 42.5 lakh, amounting to over 97.7% of his known income.
ED’s investigation and evidence established the money-laundering offence against both accused, the court said. The claims by the father and daughter that construction of a property at Vijayanagar was financed by their mother, who had purchased the sites, were not supported by documentary evidence.
Yurekha was held liable as a participant in the offence because she had knowingly assisted in holding the property purchased with the proceeds of crime in her name, the court said.
Perjury case against defence witness
In a separate order, the court directed the registration of a perjury case against M Jayaram, who testified as a defence witness.
Jayaram had stated during his examination that he did not know Ramachandra. However, during cross-examination, he admitted they were related and acknowledged that his earlier statement was false.

briefs.headline: Greater Bengaluru Authority receives around 1,600 objections to tree-felling for Hebbal Short Tunnel
briefs.deck: The National Green Tribunal restrained the BDA from felling any trees till the hearing in the case challenging tree felling for the project is completed
briefs.bodyText:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has received around 1,600 objections to the proposed felling of 1,128 trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project. Meanwhile, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has restrained the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) from felling any trees until the hearing of a petition challenging the tree felling is completed.
The GBA invited objections to the proposed tree-felling on September 20, providing a 10-day deadline. However, the authority did not upload the list of tree species, prompting activists to demand an extension.
According to the GBA sources, more than 700 objections were received during the first window, with the remaining submissions coming in before the final deadline.
An officer told The Hindu that the key concerns raised in the objections related to species diversity and the large number of trees proposed to be felled. “Many objections are very detailed and include lists of species to highlight biodiversity. Others focus on a specific aspect, such as the microclimate, and elaborate on the impact that tree felling could have on it,” the officer said.
Biodiversity loss and more
According to the officer, several objections also relate to the size of certain trees, based on independent assessments carried out by those who submitted them. Other objections raise concerns about the impact on biodiversity, hydrological issues arising from the alignment’s proximity to Hebbal Lake, and the risk of the area turning into a heat island, given its role as a key lung space.
The officer said the objections were being filtered and grouped under different themes. “We will forward all the objections and concerns raised by citizens to the tree expert committee and the implementing agency, the BDA. The BDA will also examine the objections and explain why the trees need to be felled. A joint inspection of the site will be carried out by members of the tree expert committee and the BDA to review the proposal,” he said.
Meanwhile, following an NGT stay order, the BDA cannot fell any trees until December 15, the next date of hearing. Any further action will depend on the outcome of the hearing.
Tree committee to decide
Recently, during an interaction with The Hindu, BDA Chairperson N.A. Haris said that only 56 trees would be felled and the remaining trees would be translocated. However, the GBA officer clarified that any decision regarding the trees would have to be taken by the tree expert committee.
“Irrespective of whether the trees are translocated or felled, the BDA will have to plant 10 trees for every tree cleared,” the GBA official said.

briefs.headline: Police permission sought for over 60 RSS marches across Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The RSS march applications became a talking point after Home Minister Priyank Kharge took to social media to share two communications from the RSS that “informed” the police of the proposed marches in the city.
briefs.bodyText:
Ahead of their Vijayadashami route marches on October 25, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has submitted over 60 applications across the city, and the Bengaluru police are granting permissions to those that comply with standard procedures.
The RSS march applications became a talking point after Home Minister Priyank Kharge took to social media to share two communications from the RSS that “informed” the police of the proposed marches in the city. He said the RSS had to seek “permission” rather than merely “inform” the police.
Mr. Kharge stressed the need for the police to make arrangements for logistics, food, traffic management, and other requirements, as the rallies involve lakhs of participants across the State.
However, his statement drew flak, as it was seen as another face-off between Mr. Kharge and the RSS, recalling the initial denial of permission for a route march in November 2025 in the Chittapur constituency, which Mr. Kharge represents. The controversy, however, ended after the court intervened and permission was eventually granted with specific conditions.
This time, however, Mr. Kharge brought the context as he cited the Akhil Bharatiya Pratinidhi Sabha Annual Report 2025–26 to point out that over two lakh “uninformed participants” took part in more than 562 route marches in Karnataka. He said arrangements for such large gatherings were necessary; thus, prior “approval” is needed, not “information.”
Accordingly, the Bengaluru city police are now granting permissions for applications filed in accordance with the rules.
A senior police officer told The Hindu that most of the applications had been cleared for permission. “No extra or specific directions are being followed for RSS applications. Organisers have been asked to seek permission through the standard application procedure for large gatherings, and only those marches are being granted permission,” the officer said.
Police sources said applicants were directed to submit applications clearly stating the name of the organiser and at least five volunteers, along with their contact information.
“Further, they have to furnish the approximate number of participants, a route map, the reason for the marches, and the type of march.” If these details are provided, permissions are being granted,” the officer said.

He said India could also emerge as an important export base for…
stories.bodyText:
BERLIN: German companies are exploring investment opportunities in India in precision engineering, aerospace, defence and shipbuilding, besides healthcare, pharmaceuticals and research and development, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, pointing to growing business interest as European firms look to diversify manufacturing and supply chains.
Talking to reporters during his visit to Germany and The Netherlands with a delegation of Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation, Goyal said German companies had publicly announced investments worth $7.4 billion in India with some of these already materialising.
More than 2,000 German companies currently operate in India, while cumulative German FDI equity inflows stood at $15.6 billion between April 2000 and March 2026.
“With all the regulatory overhang that they (EU) are creating upon themselves, European manufacturing will have to look for trusted partner countries where many of the things that are becoming very expensive in Europe can be produced. So I see tremendous potential for India and huge job creation in India,” Goyal said.
He said India could also emerge as an important export base for automobiles.

stories.headline: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
stories.deck: PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.
PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.
The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.
”
India ranked ninth globally among services displaying PHP information.
PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.
The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.
Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.
CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, a security researcher at CloudSEK.

stories.headline: Coforge net profit rises 56.5% as ‘record’ deal wins boost growth
stories.deck: September-quarter revenue climbs 53.6% to ₹6,171 crore; fresh order intake doubles year-on-year to $1.04 billion as company raises FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16%
stories.bodyText:
Coforge Ltd’s net profit rose 56.5% year-on-year to ₹588.1 crore in the September quarter, as the mid-tier IT services company signed a record eight large deals and reported strong revenue growth. The quarter marked its first full quarter of consolidating Encora’s financial results following the acquisition.
Revenue for the second quarter of FY27 grew 53.6% year-on-year to ₹6,170.8 crore. In dollar terms, revenue rose 40.1% to $652.2 million. Organic revenue growth was 3.8% sequentially in constant-currency terms.
Coforge’s earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose 67.8% year-on-year to ₹984.7 crore, while its EBIT margin increased to 16% from 14.6% a year earlier. The company raised its consolidated EBIT margin guidance for FY27 to 16% from 15.5% earlier. It expects its reported EBIT margin to reach 17% in the fourth quarter.
Record deal wins
The company’s fresh order intake reached $1.04 billion during the quarter, up 102% year-on-year and 50.6% sequentially. It signed eight large deals, the highest number in a single quarter in its history, the company said. One of the deals was a $230-million UK public-sector engagement signed in July 2026.
Coforge’s executable order book for the next 12 months rose 45.4% year-on-year to an all-time high of $2.38 billion.
“Our increasing large deal velocity offers assurance of sustained robust growth in the future as well,” Sudhir Singh, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, said during the earnings call.
The company hopes to sign eight or more large deals in the current quarter, Mr. Singh said. He added that most of its large deals were sole-sourced and driven by proactive solutions designed around individual enterprises’ operating needs.
AI and margins
Coforge is using artificial intelligence both to develop client solutions and to improve its own delivery processes. AI-led engineering, data integration and cloud services accounted for 86% of consolidated revenue during the quarter, according to the company.
Mr. Singh said AI was putting pressure on traditional technology-services pricing models as automation reduced the labour required to deliver projects.
“We believe that AI is breaking the link between scale and margin leadership for the tech services industry,” he said.
“Time and material, effort-based economics face pressure as automation reduces labour content,” he added.
The company expects AI-led efficiencies in its internal operations and client delivery to support profitability. During the earnings call, management said efficiencies from AI in fixed-price contracts should begin to show up in its margin numbers in the fourth quarter.
Encora integration
Mr. Singh said margin expansion at Encora was ahead of the acquisition plan and that Coforge expected the acquired business’s revenue growth to mirror that of the parent company from the third quarter onwards. The company did not quantify Encora’s contribution to the quarter’s year-on-year revenue growth.
Coforge added 1,137 employees during the quarter, taking its total headcount to 47,365. Utilisation stood at 82.4%, while trailing 12-month attrition, excluding the business process services unit, was 10.4%.
UnearthInsight, an IT industry research and advisory firm, said Coforge’s strong deal wins and acquisition-led expansion, including Encora, were supporting its growth alongside organic expansion and new-client wins. However, it cautioned that sequential growth could moderate in Q3, with the conversion of its deal pipeline into revenue determining how much growth the company could sustain through the rest of FY27.

briefs.headline: Infosys ADRs tumble 6% as growth guidance cut to 1-2%
briefs.deck: Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries. “We have seen different client-specific situations in both retail and high-tech. This is not happening across all industries. We continue to see strong growth and discretionary spending in financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing,” he said.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Infosys had a lacklustre Q2, with its shares falling 6% in early trade on the NYSE after it cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% in constant currency terms from 1.5%-3% earlier. This is the company’s weakest growth outlook in seven years, reflecting subdued volumes, pricing pressure and weakness in its mainstay market, North America, which declined 1.5% year on year.
The slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7% year on year, respectively, in constant currency terms.
Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries. “We have seen different client-specific situations in both retail and high-tech. This is not happening across all industries. We continue to see strong growth and discretionary spending in financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing,” he said.
CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka said volumes remained subdued, while competitive intensity and clients’ higher productivity expectations had put pressure on pricing. 
Discretionary spending in retail and high-tech was also lower than anticipated, he said, adding that these factors had led to the guidance cut.
Retail was additionally affected by a larger thirdparty component in the previous quarters, creating an unfavourable sequential comparison. While weakness in high-tech and retail was broadly similar across geographies, the impact was more pronounced in the US, Sanghrajka said.
The company retained its operating margin guidance at 20%-22% for FY27.
In dollar terms, Infosys’ revenue rose 1.2% sequentially and 1.3% year on year to $5.1 billion in the September quarter. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% year on year. AI was a bright spot, accounting for 10.5% of revenue and growing 29% sequentially, compared with 8.2% in the previous quarter, Parekh said.

briefs.headline: Driven by travel, outward transfers jump 6% to $2.7 billion
briefs.deck: Business travel surged 365.4% to $51 million from $11 million, while other travel, including leisure trips and international credit card settlements, fell 7.4% to $713.8 million. Spending on pilgrimage travel declined 46% to $5.5 million and remittances for travel-related medical treatment fell 17.7% to $4.5 million. Investments in foreign equity and debt instruments fell 6.7% from July to $321.5…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Outward remittances under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 6% month-on-month to $2.7 billion in Aug 2026, driven by overseas student travel, business travel and payments for remote education, while investments in foreign equity and debt more than doubled from a year earlier.
Travel accounted for 59.5% of total remittances, rising 11.4% from July to $1.6 billion. Within this, remittances for overseas education travel, including fees and hostel expenses, rose 28.5% to $855.5 million from $665.8 million.
Business travel surged 365.4% to $51 million from $11 million, while other travel, including leisure trips and international credit card settlements, fell 7.4% to $713.8 million. Spending on pilgrimage travel declined 46% to $5.5 million and remittances for travel-related medical treatment fell 17.7% to $4.5 million.
Investments in foreign equity and debt instruments fell 6.7% from July to $321.5 million but were 111.3% higher than in Aug 2025.
Remittances for maintenance of close relatives declined 2.8% month-on-month to $275.4 million, while gifts fell 6.8% to $215.7 million. Both categories recorded annual increases of 1.2% and 13.3%, respectively.
Remittances for remote and distance education rose 29.2% to $191.8 million from July but were 39.9% lower than a year earlier. This category covers educational services consumed remotely, including correspondence courses and online degree programmes, rather than expenses involving physical travel abroad.
Deposits abroad rose 8.8% monthon-month to $50.8 million and were 18.8% higher year-on-year. Remittances for overseas property purchases fell 22.2% to $39.6 million from July but were 9.9% higher than a year earlier. Other remittances declined 13.3% to $8.1 million, while payments for remote medical treatment rose 23.2% to $4.8 million. Donations fell 34.2% to $0.5 million.

briefs.headline: India seventh most targeted by cyberattacks: MS executive Nicholas Butts
briefs.deck: Butts cited Storm 3168, also called Jadepuffer, which he described as a China-based ransomware operation using AI agents against customers worldwide. He also pointed to Russian and Chinese state-sponsored actors deploying agents for espionage, including a group Microsoft tracks as Storm 0940. AI was also lowering the barriers for smaller criminal operations, he said.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India is the world’s seventh most targeted country by cyberattacks and third in Asia, a senior Microsoft executive said Friday, warning that artificial intelligence was already helping criminals mount ransomware and espionage campaigns.
At the NDTV World Summit 2026, Nicholas Butts, director of AI and cybersecurity policy at Microsoft, said the risks were immediate.
“What we’re seeing is not about potential doom and gloom in 10 years but about very real security threats right here today,” he said.
Butts cited Storm 3168, also called Jadepuffer, which he described as a China-based ransomware operation using AI agents against customers worldwide.
He also pointed to Russian and Chinese state-sponsored actors deploying agents for espionage, including a group Microsoft tracks as Storm 0940.
AI was also lowering the barriers for smaller criminal operations, he said.
Butts cited EvilTokens, allegedly built by two individuals using AI coding tools, which offered access to criminal infrastructure and affected more than 10,000 organisations across 120 countries. He did not specify how many were Indian.
“The threat is very real to India,” Butts said. Microsoft’s assessment draws on its extensive security monitoring, including screening about five billion emails daily, he added.

briefs.headline: At $43 billion, RBI’s net dollar purchase hits new high
briefs.deck: India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion in the week ended Oct 16, down $64.7 billion from their all-time high of $785.71 billion in the week ended Sept 4, as pressure on the rupee continued. Foreign currency assets, the largest component of reserves, declined by $5.76 billion during the latest week. The fall was partly offset by a $706 million increase in the…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: RBI’s net dollar purchases surged 132% to $43.3 billion in Aug 2026, driven by inflows through its concessional FCNR(B) swap facility, while its outstanding net forward short position crossed $200 billion for the first time.
RBI bought $74.5 billion in dollars during the month, up 93.9% from $38.4 billion in July. It made no dollar purchases in Aug 2025, when it was defending the rupee amid foreign portfolio outflows. Dollar sales rose 57.9% month-on-month to $31.2 billion from $19.8 billion in July and were 305.6% higher than the $7.7 billion sold in Aug 2025.
Surges 132% In Aug Driven By FCNR Flows,Forward Liabilities Rise Too, Cross $200Bn
Net purchases were 132% higher than the $18.7 billion recorded in July and contrasted with net sales of $7.7 billion in Aug 2025. Gross transactions across onshore and offshore over-the-counter markets exceeded $105.7 billion. RBI’s dollar purchases helped absorb the $127 billion mobilised by banks through FCNR(B) deposits from NRIs.
However, pressure on the rupee prompted the central bank to sell dollars to support the currency. Its dollar sales of $31.2 billion in Aug represented around a quarter of the amount mobilised through FCNR(B) deposits, though the two figures cover different types of transactions and periods of currency management.
India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion in the week ended Oct 16, down $64.7 billion from their all-time high of $785.71 billion in the week ended Sept 4, as pressure on the rupee continued. Foreign currency assets, the largest component of reserves, declined by $5.76 billion during the latest week. The fall was partly offset by a $706 million increase in the value of gold reserves.
RBI’s concessional dollar-rupee swap facility allowed banks to exchange dollar deposits raised from NRIs for three to five years for rupees, while securing forward hedges from the central bank. The deposit mobilisation window closed at the end of Aug, prompting banks to surrender the dollar proceeds to RBI.
The central bank also stepped up dollar sales and conducted offsetting sellbuy swaps to manage the rupee and the liquidity injected through its purchases. Its outstanding net forward short position rose by $63.3 billion, or 46.3%, in a month to a record $200.1 billion at end-Aug, compared with $136.8 billion in July and $53.4 billion a year earlier.

During the day’s session, 
sensex
 fluctuated by more than 1,300 points but closed just 126 points down at 73,124 points. 
Nifty
 on NSE also witnessed strong volatility and closed 88 points lower at 22,600 points, mainly because of foreign fund buying in the latter half of the session, market players said. Outside of the main indices, BSE’s midcap index closed 2.2% lower while the smallcap index closed 2.5%.

According to Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments, the key concern in Friday’s market was the disproportionately sharp correction in mid and smallcap stocks relative to the leading indices. “Valuation concerns and unwinding of leveraged positions, combined with surging crude prices and weak global cues, have intensified pressure on the broader market. briefs.headline: Record haul: Jio IPO collects Rs 7.5 lakh crore; nearly 1.3 crore investors make bids
briefs.deck: In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,370, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of about Rs 250 over the upper limit of the IPO price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119. briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, which aimed to raise a recordbreaking Rs 30,213 crore, on Friday created several other records. It saw about 1.3 crore retail investors participating in the offer. While the institutional part was subscribed more than 70 times, the total demand for shares, including the anchor part in the offer, touched almost Rs 7.5 lakh crore.
The earlier record for applications in an IPO was for Waaree Energies in which a little over 97 lakh investors had applied. In 2008, the Reliance Power IPO had seen the total demand at about Rs 7.1 lakh crore. At Friday’s close of bidding, Jio IPO surpassed both these marks.
On Day 1, India’s biggest IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening, exchange data had shown. By Day 2, the issue was subscribed more than five times. And at the close of Day 3, the last day of the bidding process, the IPO was subscribed 22.2 times, exchange data showed. At close, the institutional (QIB) part of the IPO, in which a little over 4.9 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 70.6 times, while the HNI portion, in which about 3.6 crore shares were reserved, was subscribed 14 times.
Nearly 1.3Cr Investors Make Bids; Institutions Lead Charge
Exchange data also showed that the portion reserved for Jio employees was subscribed nearly three times while the part reserved for RIL shareholders was subscribed 7.6 times. The portion marked for retail investors, in which about 8.5 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 2.7 times.
In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,370, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of about Rs 250 over the upper limit of the IPO price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119. The current GMP is slightly off Rs 273, the highest level seen a day before the IPO opened. However, the latest GMP is much higher than the opening quote of Rs 148 on Oct 4, data from websites tracking the price trend in the unofficial market for shares showed.
The strong response to the IPO comes on the back of a Rs 2.5-lakh-crore anchor book that was subscribed 30 times its size, which was Rs 8,110 crore, disclosures by the merchant bankers to the issue showed.

Core inflation rose to 4.3%, while core inflation excluding precious metals reached 3.2%. WPI inflation climbed to 11.4% under the 2022-23 base series. The report highlighted early signs of inflation generalisation, with a rising share…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: RBI’s Oct 2026 State of the Economy report flagged rising inflation, geopolitical tensions and global financial volatility as key risks to India’s growth outlook, even as strong domestic demand, services activity and exports supported economic momentum.
The report said headline CPI inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% in Sept from 4.8% in Aug, with price increases spreading across food, fuel and core items. Core inflation rose to 4.3%, while core inflation excluding precious metals reached 3.2%. WPI inflation climbed to 11.4% under the 2022-23 base series. The report highlighted early signs of inflation generalisation, with a rising share of CPI items recording inflation above 6%.
The report said deficient rainfall in some regions could adversely affect kharif crop yields. However, rice and wheat stocks stood at 3.3 times the quarterly buffer norm as of Oct 1, providing a cushion against supply disruptions. Higher minimum support prices announced on Sept 30 for the 2027-28 rabi marketing season were intended to ensure remunerative prices and incentivise crop diversification.

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
Globally, the IMF outlook remained subject to downside risks, including the West Asia conflict, trade tensions, high sovereign bond yields, elevated public debt and concerns over fiscal sustainability. 
The global growth projection for 2027 assumed the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in March and a broad return to pre-war conditions by Oct 2027. The report identified positive technology shocks and gains from artificial intelligence as potential offsets to the global slowdown.
The report highlighted mounting global financial risks as geopolitical frictions in West Asia intensified inflationary pressures and disrupted supply chains. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies raised concerns about fiscal sustainability and financial stability, particularly amid debt and fiscal pressures in France and the US.

briefs.headline: IndusInd Bank posts profit of ₹1,242 crores in Q2; asset quality improvement and interest income drives growth
briefs.deck: The bank’s bottom line for Q2FY27 was supported by a rise in net interest income, which stood at ₹4,569 crore as against ₹4,409 crores a year ago
briefs.bodyText:
IndusInd Bank Limited posted a net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the quarter ended September, up 20% sequentially and trimming net loss of ₹437 for the same quarter in the preceding year. The bank had incurred net loss for the same period in previous year due to an increase in microfinance provisioning and write-offs.
The bank’s bottom line for Q2FY27 was supported by a rise in net interest income, which stood at ₹4,569 crore as against ₹4,409 crores a year ago. Sequentially, interest income declined by 2%. NII for half year (H1FY27) rose to ₹9,254, up 2.3% on year.
Asset quality of the bank improved substantially, with gross non-performing assets (NPA) ratio at 2.73% compared to 3.60% on year and net NPA declining to 0.83% from 1.04% in Q2FY26. However, the net interest margin of the bank slipped to 3.23% from 3.32% a year ago.
Net revenue of the bank for the period rose to ₹6,817 crores compared to ₹6,00 crores a year. A decline in operating expenses also helped push the bottom-line numbers, with expenses slipping to ₹3,943 crores in July-Septemeber from ₹4,013 crore for the same period last year.
Deposits of the bank rose 10% year-on-year to ₹4.28 crores. Advances of the bank for the period stood at 3.63 crores.
IndusInd held provisions of $9,012 crore as of September 30, with the provision coverage ratio at 70%.
IndusInd Bank raised nearly $3.5 billion via the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) account, which was impacted the contraction in NIM. The bank said recovery in margin related to FCNR-B is expected over the next two quarters.
“Q2 reflects the growing strength of the IndusInd Bank franchise and the progress we have made in rebuilding momentum across the business. Our Q2 results demonstrate that the growth has strengthened, profitability has improved, asset quality trends remain encouraging, and our funding profile is becoming more granular and resilient,” Rajiv Anand, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of IndusInd Bank said.
Also read | IndusInd bank’s Q1FY27 PAT up 47% on lower provisions
The bank also informed the exchanges on Friday (October 23, 2026) that the Board of Directors of the lender has appointed Priyanka Sinha as an Additional Director in the category of Non-Executive Independent Director for a period of four consecutive years, till October 22, 2030.
Speaking to the media at post-earnings conference call, the bank said it remains confident of reaching a 1% exit return on assets for FY27. Bank also expects loans growth momentum to continue driven by retail and wholesale lending. Shares of IndusInd Bank Ltd closed at ₹835.00 on Friday, down 1.76%, on the BSE.

stories.headline: IND A vs NZ A: KL Rahul, Sai, Jaiswal fail to fire as India A all out for 113
stories.bodyText:
India A's bowlers have a huge task ahead after the team's batting line-up managed just 113 runs in the first innings of the opening unofficial Test against New Zealand A.
India A's bowlers must now deliver. With only a modest total to defend, they will need early wickets to stop New Zealand A from taking control of the match. Striking in the opening overs and building pressure through disciplined bowling will be crucial if India A are to make a contest of it.
India A's first innings lasted less than two sessions as New Zealand A's fast bowlers exploited the helpful conditions to dismiss the visitors for just 113.
After winning the toss and opting to bowl, New Zealand A made full use of the grass on the pitch. Fraser Sheat provided the early breakthrough by removing KL Rahul, but Yashasvi Jaiswal and Devdutt Padikkal offered some resistance with a partnership before Zak Gibson ended Jaiswal's stay.
Simon Keene then caused further damage with a superb spell of bowling. He extracted movement from the surface and claimed five wickets, leaving India A's batting line-up struggling to build any momentum.
With wickets falling at regular intervals, Yash Rathod took the fight to the New Zealand A bowlers. He attacked whenever an opportunity came his way and kept the scoreboard moving even as partners departed at the other end.
Rathod also put together a valuable last-wicket partnership with Mukesh Choudhary, doing most of the scoring to take India A beyond the 100-run mark. However, the late resistance could not prevent the visitors from being dismissed for a modest total of 113.
India A are in desperate need of runs, and Yash Rathod is fighting back with an aggressive display of batting.
With India A reduced to 95/9, Rathod took on Fraser Sheat in the 39th over, smashing three sixes to collect 18 runs. He pulled a short delivery over deep square leg, flicked another over fine leg and hammered a third over the boundary to take India A past the 100-run mark.
Rathod moved to 44 off 49 balls, bringing some much-needed runs for the visitors. He also struck a four in the previous over against Simon Keene, who had already picked up four wickets.
India A reached 113/9 after 39 overs, with Mukesh Choudhary at the other end on zero. Rathod is closing in on a valuable half-century as India A look to add as many runs as possible with their last wicket standing.
New Zealand A won the toss and elected to bowl, and the decision appeared to be paying off early.
KL Rahul failed to make an impact, falling for a duck after facing eight balls.
Fraser Sheat struck the first blow, dismissing Rahul with a catch behind the stumps. The delivery was pitched up around off-stump and swung away. Rahul went for an expansive drive away from his body without much foot movement and edged it to wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay, who took a safe catch.
Squads
India A: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Ravichandran Smaran, Dhruv Jurel (captain and wicketkeeper), Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper), Washington Sundar, Auqib Nabi, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Manav Suthar, Mukesh Choudhary, Sai Sudarsan, Yash Rathod, Mukesh Kumar.
New Zealand A: Rhys Mariu (captain), Matt Boyle, Max Chu, Kristian Clarke, Dean Foxcroft, Zak Gibson, Mitch Hay (wicketkeeper), Curtis Heaphy, Simon Keene, Jayden Lennox, Jarrod McKay, Tim Robinson, Fraser Sheat.
New Zealand A will also look to test their players against an experienced Indian line-up.
New Zealand on Friday named an extended 19-member squad featuring 11 current and former international players for the three four-day matches against India A.
Canterbury's Rhys Mariu will captain the team in the first two matches. The captain for the third game will be announced later.
The squad includes Adi Ashok, Kristian Clarke, Dean Foxcroft, Matt Fisher, Mitch Hay, Jayden Lennox, Ben Lister, Henry Nicholls and Tim Robinson, who have represented New Zealand at the international level.
The schedule could affect the availability of some senior players for the entire India A series. India's three-match ODI series against New Zealand begins on November 4.
The second and third unofficial Tests are scheduled to be played in Christchurch from October 31 to November 3 and in Lincoln from November 7 to 10.
India senior team's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak highlighted the importance of the three unofficial Tests, saying the matches would benefit both established Test players and those waiting for opportunities.
"There is a lot of importance of India A series. Because, a lot of Test players, a lot of fringe players, those who are waiting for their opportunity, it is also very good for them.
"And, before the Test series, see, even the senior players, somewhere or the other, the match practice of the red ball is very important. So, all in all, the setup that has been done, which the BCCI has kept with the India A Series, will definitely help the team," Kotak told reporters.
Akash Deep, who is also part of India's Test squad, will look to build his rhythm and match fitness during the series.
Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant will miss the match as he continues his recovery at the BCCI Centre of Excellence.
Kumar Kushagra replaced Pant in the squad for the first two matches of the tour after Pant suffered a left-side strain while leading the Rest of India team in the Irani Cup.
A decision on Pant's availability for the third match will be taken later. Captain Jurel is also available as a wicketkeeping option.
India A will look to make the most of the four-day opening match against New Zealand A, beginning on Saturday in Lincoln, as the visitors prepare for next month's two-Test series.
Led by wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel, India A will play at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval. The match will give the players valuable exposure to local conditions ahead of India's World Test Championship (WTC) assignment, which begins on November 19 in Wellington.
KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal are among the prominent names in the squad. Other key players include Devdutt Padikkal, Washington Sundar, Sai Sudharsan and pacers Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj and Mukesh Kumar.

stories.headline: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Rauf on need for bigger totals
stories.deck: Haris Rauf said his role alongside Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah is to take wickets and strengthen Pakistan’s bowling attack. He stressed teamwork, middle-over breakthroughs and the need for bigger totals as ODI cricket becomes more aggressive. Rauf is also focusing on improving his pace and fitness, while backing Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to contribute runs in upcoming matches.
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has explained his role alongside 
Shaheen Shah Afridi
 and 
Naseem Shah
, saying their main job is to take important wickets and help the team win matches.
Speaking to the media in Lahore, Rauf highlighted the importance of teamwork as Pakistan look to continue their strong performance in the ongoing ODI tri-series.
“My role, along with Naseem and Shaheen, is to take wickets for the team. This is a team game, and everyone is supporting one another,” Rauf said.
He also praised Shaheen’s presence in the bowling attack, saying his inclusion gives Pakistan an added advantage.
“Having Shaheen in the team is always beneficial,” he added.
Pakistan’s bowling plans and growing run rates
Pakistan have started the tri-series well, winning their opening matches against Sri Lanka and England. Rauf said successfully defending a total of 300 runs was encouraging, but teams now need to score more runs because modern-day cricket has become more aggressive.
“Defending 300 runs is a good sign. Our effort is to ensure that the bowling unit continues to perform well. When teams are scoring more than 300 or 400 runs, we also have to think about posting totals of 350 and defending them,” he said.
Rauf also stressed that taking wickets during the middle overs is important to stop opposition batters from scoring freely and building strong partnerships.
“You have to take wickets in the middle overs. Wherever you play in the world, runs are scored because cricket has changed,” he remarked.
Rauf focuses on pace as Pakistan prepare for England
Rauf believes fast bowlers remain a major weapon in modern cricket. He said he is working on improving his fitness and speed to become more effective for Pakistan, while keeping his attention on performances rather than criticism.
“A fast bowler is an X-factor in today’s cricket. I continue to work on my fitness and pace so that I can give people fewer reasons to talk,” he said.
The pacer also backed Pakistan batters Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to deliver important contributions in the remaining matches.
After beating Sri Lanka and England, Pakistan will return to action against England in the fourth match of the tri-series at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday, following a two-day break.
The team will aim to maintain its winning momentum with strong performances from both its batting and bowling units.

stories.headline: Australia face selection headaches after 'shambolic' South Africa defeat
stories.deck: Australia collapsed to 99 all out in their first innings and were then dismissed for 295, with a superb 121 from Travis Head and defiant 40 off 166 balls by nightwatchman Scott Boland the only highlights
stories.bodyText:
Australia captain Pat Cummins admits it is hard to "paper over the cracks" after a thumping second Test defeat to South Africa, with the fate of at least three players hanging in the balance.
The visitors crashed by an innings and 31 runs at St. George's Park in Gqeberha on Thursday (October 22, 2026) to leave the three-Test series finely poised at 1-1 heading into the decider at Cape Town next week.
Australia collapsed to 99 all out in their first innings and were then dismissed for 295, with a superb 121 from Travis Head and defiant 40 off 166 balls by nightwatchman Scott Boland the only highlights.
The manner of the heavy loss did not go down well in Australia, with headlines ranging from "horror show" to "shambolic Aussies" and "brutal failures laid bare".
"Clearly need to be a lot better than that if we want to compete," Cummins said.
"I think a loss can sometimes kick you into gear. You can maybe paper over the cracks sometimes in a win. Whereas I think in a loss, it makes you ask questions as a player of yourself."
Heading into the third Test, there are question marks around at least three players, not least the underperforming Marnus Labuschagne who has gone three years without a Test century.
"He's actually doing the hard bit, he's getting to 30," Cummins said of number three Labuschagne.
"I think he's got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores — 30s aren't going to win you many matches.
"So, again, we'll work on that in the next couple of days. It's one Test match left in the series, we've got to win this."
Recently-recalled opener Nic Maddinson is also on shaky ground after scores of 0, 48, 0 and 8 across the first two Tests, while all-rounder Beau Webster appears vulnerable.
Cameron Green is expected to be available for Cape Town after injury sidelined him from the first two Tests while Josh Inglis is also fit. Cooper Connolly is another option.
Paceman Boland, who came into the side at Gqeberha at the expense of spinner Nathan Lyon, will be hard to drop given his batting exploits and a five-wicket haul in the first innings.
Much will depend on the nature of the Cape Town pitch on whether Australia again opt for four seamers or Lyon is brought back.
Cummins admitted some hard decisions would have to be made.
"That's the challenge. Do you give someone one more game, or do you feel like now is the right time to make a move?" he said.
"Does it feel like someone's just about to turn the corner, and they're going to be away, or does it now feel like the right time for a change-up?"

stories.headline: India wins historic first mixed doubles medal at Asian TT in 72 years
stories.deck: After taking the opening game 11-6, the Indians lost the next two, leaving themselves under enormous pressure. However, the duo responded impressively, winning the fourth game 11-9 before holding their nerve to clinch the decider by the same margin
stories.bodyText:
Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade ensured India's first mixed doubles medal at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in 72 years by reaching the semifinals here on Friday (October 24, 2026).
The Indian pair battled past South Korea’s Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun 3–2 (11-6, 8-11, 8-11, 11-9, 11-9) in a gripping quarterfinal to secure at least bronze.
After taking the opening game 11-6, the Indians lost the next two, leaving themselves under enormous pressure. However, the duo responded impressively, winning the fourth game 11-9 before holding their nerve to clinch the decider by the same margin.
The Indians next face Japan’s Miwa Harimoto and Sora Matsushima in the semifinals.
The five-game victory underlined the pair’s resilience and ability to recover when the match threatened to slip away. Harmeet and Yashaswini had progressed to the quarterfinals with a 3-1 win over Chinese Taipei and Indonesia (3-0) in the preceding round, after enjoying a first-round bye.
The achievement marks a significant moment for Indian table tennis. India’s previous mixed doubles medals at the Asian Championships came in 1952, when Gool Nasikwala and Kalyan Jayant won gold, and in 1954, when Yatin Vyas and Meena Parande secured silver.

briefs.headline: Rajesh Bhandari appointed acting president at EC meeting; Ajay Singh camp rejects proceedings
briefs.deck: A faction opposed to the president of the Boxing Federation of India claims significant changes occurred recently. This faction announced the revocation of secretary general Pramod Kumar's suspension and appointed Rajesh Bhandari as acting president. They stated these resolutions were passed during a recent executive committee meeting in New Delhi. However, the federation's executive director…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In a fresh escalation of the power struggle within the Boxing Federation of India (BFI), a faction opposed to president 
Ajay Singh
 has claimed that eight executive committee (EC) members have endorsed its decisions, revoked secretary general 
Pramod Kumar
’s suspension and appointed senior vice-president Rajesh Bhandari as acting president.
The group said the resolutions were passed at an EC meeting held recently in the Capital, ahead of the Oct 28 special general meeting (SGM) where a no-confidence motion against Singh is scheduled to be considered.
However, BFI executive director Col (retd) Arun Malik rejected the meeting and its decisions, saying the federation had not issued any notice in accordance with its constitution. “The BFI constitution expressly requires the date, venue and agenda of an EC meeting to be confirmed by the president and requires meetings to be convened under the president’s advice,” Malik told TOI, adding that Singh had not been notified.
Malik asserted that BFI did not recognise Bhandari’s appointment or any resolutions passed at the purported meeting.
Those listed as present at the EC were vice-presidents Leonardo Daniel Oliver D Gama and Bhandari, Kumar, treasurer Pon Bhaskaran, joint secretaries Swapan Banerjee and Teli Khai, and executive members Pheiroijam Dhanajit Singh and Kamal Ch Goyary. Bhaskaran attended online.
The minutes state that the committee unanimously approved the proposed no-confidence motion for consideration and voting by the general body. 
It also revoked Kumar’s suspension, endorsed the formation of a constitution committee and approved Bhandari’s appointment as acting president, citing D Gama’s health issues. The resolutions further challenged the constitutional amendments adopted at the Aug 27 SGM, alleging that state units’ consent had been obtained under duress.
Malik defended the Aug constitutional amendments, saying they were approved by the general body with the requisite quorum and overwhelming majority, subsequently published on BFI’s official websites and notified to World Boxing.
The confrontation follows the suspension of Kumar by Singh and the secretary general’s subsequent counter-order against the president. Kumar’s faction has alleged governance and administrative irregularities, while Singh’s camp has questioned the validity of the proposed no-confidence process.

briefs.headline: Will Ishan's injury be Sooryavanshi's gain? 15-year-old in contention for 2nd T20I
briefs.deck: Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I match against New Zealand due to a strain. The team management has added uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra as a replacement in the squad. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may finally get an opportunity to play after being on the sidelines for nine matches. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak emphasized the need for patience regarding Sooryavanshi's…
briefs.bodyText:
One game into India’s tour of New Zealand and the familiar fitness concerns have already surfaced. Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during the series opener on Thursday. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak revealed that Ishan was pushed down the order in the first T20I because of the injury. While a BCCI statement said the medical team is monitoring his progress, no timeline has been given for his return. Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra was added to the squad as cover.
The setback could finally pave the way for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has spent the last nine matches on the sidelines. The team management, led by head coach Gautam Gambhir, has resisted calls to fast-track the 15-yearold despite the clamour around his talent. With uncertainty over Ishan’s recovery, however, the teenager may now get an opportunity in conditions far more challenging than those at home.
Sooryavanshi attended an optional training session on Friday alongside Abhishek Sharma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Varun Chakravarthy, Shivam Dube and Kuldeep Yadav. 
Under Kotak’s watchful eye, he spent considerable time in the nets, a clear indication that the team wants him ready if needed. If the team management decides to veer away from their template of playing eight batters and field a spinner, Sooryavanshi may have to wait.
Few young cricketers in recent years have generated as much excitement a s Sooryavanshi. His exploits in the IPL and age-group cricket have fuelled expectations, with fans, experts and social media all eager to see him in India colours more regularly. Yet the management feels patience will benefit him more than premature exposure. The challenge in New Zealand will be significantly different: larger grounds, movement off the pitch and through the air, and a minuscule margin for error. The examination could be sterner than what he has encountered so far.
Kotak believes the teenager has already matured since first joining the national setup. “Now, he is much more mature. He understood why he is not playing. He has never complained. He is working on his fielding and fitness and is constantly observing others’ batting. The lessons you learn at this level are very different, and he has to absorb those too,” Kotak said.
While acknowledging the popularity surrounding the youngster, Kotak cautioned against allowing public sentiment to dictate team selection. “Everyone likes him. The public likes him. Social media likes him. The team likes him. But you can’t make changes in the XI just because people like a player. He will learn a lot once he starts playing, but initially there was too much hype around his place in the side,” he said.
“I genuinely felt that wasn’t good for the player either. For a 15-year-old, everyone saying he must play doesn’t leave him much space. He is still very young. It’s unfair on other players who are performing as well. People involved in cricket should think whether they are helping or simply creating noise.”
Sooryavanshi has already captured the imagination of fans through his IPL exploits. If selected, the next step will be proving he can thrive when the conditions are far less forgiving.

briefs.headline: Shreyas Iyer on verge of breaking Rohit Sharma's unique T20I captaincy record
briefs.deck: Iyer, who took over as India's T20I captain from Suryakumar Yadav in June, has scored 632 runs in 22 matches as skipper this year.
briefs.bodyText:
Shreyas Iyer
 is closing in on a record held by 
Rohit Sharma
 and will have a chance to become India's highest run-scorer as T20I captain in a calendar year when the team faces New Zealand in the second match of the five-match series on Saturday (October 24) at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.
Iyer, who took over as India's T20I captain from Suryakumar Yadav in June, has scored 632 runs in 22 matches as skipper this year. He needs 25 runs in Saturday's match to go past Rohit's tally of 656 runs, which the former India captain scored in 29 T20Is in 2022.
Rohit led India to the T20 World Cup title in 2024. However, the record for the most runs by a captain in T20Is in a calendar year belongs to Pakistan's 
Babar Azam
, who scored 939 runs in 29 matches as skipper in 2021. Japan's Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming is second on the list, having scored 860 runs in 20 T20Is as captain in 2024.
Iyer batted at No. 4 in India's series opener against New Zealand on Thursday and scored 42 off 28 balls during the chase of 226 runs. India won the match by four wickets.
The Punjab Kings captain in the IPL also has a chance to break another record in T20 cricket this year. Iyer has scored 1,130 runs as captain across T20 matches in 2026. He needs 96 runs in Saturday's match to go past Babar's tally of 1,225 runs, which the Pakistan batter scored in 35 matches as captain in 2021.
Ishan Kishan ruled out of second T20I against New Zealand
India wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of Saturday's second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch after suffering a right adductor strain during the series opener.
Kishan's absence could open the door for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to make his debut for the senior Indian team.
The youngster last played for India during the Asian Games in Japan, where he scored 15 in the semifinal against Sri Lanka and 38 in the final against Pakistan. India went on to win its second consecutive gold medal in the event.

briefs.headline: Mona and Nishad to be India's flag-bearers at closing ceremony of Asian Para Games
briefs.deck: Both Agarwal and Kumar won two gold medals each at the Games.
briefs.bodyText:
Double gold medallists shooter Mona Agarwal and jumps specialist Nishad Kumar will be India's flag bearers at the closing ceremony of the Asian Para Games, scheduled here for Saturday (October 24, 2026).
Both Agarwal and Kumar won two gold medals each at the Games.
The 38-year-old Agarwal, who contracted polio at the age of nine, affecting both her lower limbs and leaving her dependent on a wheelchair, went on a record-breaking spree at the Games.
She first won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games record and followed it up by shattering the world record en route to gold in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 event.
The 27-year-old Nishad, whose right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Himachal Pradesh when he was six years old, clinched gold in the men's high jump and long jump T47 events.

briefs.headline: Ake Loba's brace hand East Bengal easy 5-1 win over Inter Kashi in ISL
briefs.deck: The defending champions made a dominant start, with in-form Ramírez scoring in the eighth minute. After receiving the ball on the right side of the penalty area, Ramírez lifted it over Albino Gomes to put East Bengal ahead
briefs.bodyText:
Ake Loba scored a brace as East Bengal FC produced a commanding performance to thrash Inter Kashi 5-1 in an Indian Super League match here on Friday (October 23, 2026).
Dani Ramirez, P.V. Vishnu and Lukasz Zwolinski too found the back of the net for East Bengal in a lopsided contest.
The defending champions made a dominant start, with in-form Ramírez scoring in the eighth minute. After receiving the ball on the right side of the penalty area, Ramírez lifted it over Albino Gomes to put East Bengal ahead.
The Torchbearers doubled their advantage in the 16th minute through Vishnu, who finished a swift counterattack with a left-footed strike into the bottom-left corner after being set up by Loba.
East Bengal extended their lead in the 22nd minute when Loba converted a penalty, awarded after Ramírez was brought down inside the box by Wayne Vaz. Loba fired a right-footed effort into the top-right corner to open his scoring tally for the season.
Inter Kashi pulled one back in the 28th minute after Lalchungnunga scored an own goal, giving the visitors a lifeline.
However, East Bengal continued their attacking approach, with Loba completing his brace to make it 4-1 before half-time.
With the game firmly in the Torchbearers' hands, head coach Habas substituted key players Rashid, Loba and Vipin Singh to avoid injuries and give young players some minutes at the start of the second half,
East Bengal adopted a more measured approach, prioritising possession and avoiding unnecessary risks, while Inter Kashi pressed hard in search of a way back into the contest.
Lukasz Zwolinski came off the bench and scored his first goal in the ISL for East Bengal in the 81st minute, finding the bottom-left corner with a left-footed shot from close range after Christopher Ikonomidis provided the assist.

briefs.headline: Ayush Mhatre undergoes surgery for hamstring injury, sidelined for about three months
briefs.deck: "Ayush Mhatre underwent right hamstring surgery yesterday (on Thursday) at the Kokilaben Hospital in Mumbai, performed by Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala," says BCCI source
briefs.bodyText:
India U-19 World Cup-winning skipper and Mumbai vice-captain Ayush Mhatre has undergone surgery for his right hamstring injury and is likely to remain on the sidelines for two to three months.
Mhatre had suffered a Grade 4 tear in his right hamstring while running between the wickets on the first day of Mumbai's Ranji Trophy season opener against Chandigarh in Mumbai on October 11.
It was his first game since being sidelined from a left hamstring injury during the IPL while playing for Chennai Super Kings against Sunrisers Hyderabad on April 18.
"Ayush Mhatre underwent right hamstring surgery on Thursday [October 22, 2026] at the Kokilaben Hospital in Mumbai, performed by Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala," a BCCI source told PTI.
"He is currently recovering well and is expected to take approximately 2-3 months to make a full recovery and return to competitive cricket. The surgery was successful, and as of Friday morning (October 23, 2026), Ayush even started walking slowly with crutches," the source added.
After suffering the left hamstring injury during the IPL, the 19-year-old Mhatre spent three months at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru undergoing treatment and rehabilitation.
Mhatre's injury forced Mumbai to look for a second opening pair in as many Ranji Trophy matches this season.
While Mhatre had opened with Yashasvi Jaiswal against Chandigarh, the pair of Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena opened the innings in Mumbai's away clash against Himachal Pradesh after the Indian opener left for national duties.

briefs.headline: S. Meghana retires from all forms of cricket
briefs.deck: "As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude," Meghana wrote in an Instagram post
briefs.bodyText:
India's top-order batter S. Meghana on Friday (October 23, 2026) announced her retirement from all forms of cricket at the age of 30.
Hailing from Andhra Pradesh, Meghana last played for India in November 2022. She played for RCB and Gujarat Giants in the Women's Premier League.
"As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude," Meghana wrote in an Instagram post.
"The field has been my second home, teaching me resilience, humility, and giving me memories and friendships that I will carry for a lifetime," she wrote.
"While my cricket days come to an end, my bond with cricket will never break. I will always stay deeply connected to the game and intend to dedicate my life to giving back to the sport, mentoring the next generation, and serving the game that gave me everything," she added.
She made her India T20 debut against the West Indies back in 2016. Six years later, she played her first ODI. She scored a fifty each in both the formats.

briefs.headline: Bayern Munich coach collapses after training session, taken to hospital
briefs.deck: Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club would give Kompany all the time he needed to recover, stressing that his health remained the priority.
briefs.bodyText:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalised on Friday after collapsing following a training session. The 40-year-old was observing the session when the incident occurred, the German club said.
“Kompany will undergo comprehensive examinations at the hospital and remain under medical care,” the team stated. “In the meantime, his coaching staff will manage training and match-related activities.”
Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club would give Kompany all the time he needed to recover, stressing that his health remained the priority.
“Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority,” Eberl said. “We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure that he recovers quickly. Vinnie will receive all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs.”
Kompany had previously been diagnosed with a viral infection, which forced him to miss a training session and a press conference on Tuesday. However, he returned to the dugout for Bayern's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday.
After the match, Kompany admitted that he had tried to carry on despite being unwell and had ignored the signals his body was giving him.
The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 at home against Arsenal in the Champions League earlier this week, are due to travel to Freiburg on Sunday.
Bayern are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday. The club said Kompany's coaching staff would oversee training and match-related activities while he remains under medical care.
